mission.brief: Move the incoming draft to /home/learner/Reports/report.txt. Preserve its original contents, remove the old inbox/draft.txt entry, and read the final report. A second copy without removing the old entry is incomplete.
constraints: All paths and files are virtual. Commands act immediately; there is no Apply step and no host access.
Use only the syntax in Command reference. No quotes, wildcards, shell expansion, pipes, recursion, links, archives, or unsupported options.
Relative and absolute paths are equivalent. The final state and explicitly named activity evidence earn credit; no exact transcript is required.
File-management commands may change only descendants of /home/learner. Other paths and mutation-root nodes are pinned.
Any actual filesystem change clears cat/find verification. Read or discover the final result again. Skipped no-clobber commands do not clear evidence.

objectives.label: Final state: report matches original draft content
Final state: old draft entry absent

hints: Moving changes the name/location while copying keeps both entries.
Give mv a destination filename to rename, or an existing folder to keep the basename. This simulation moves regular files only.
mv -n /home/learner/inbox/draft.txt /home/learner/Reports/report.txt, then read the new path.

/home/learner/inbox/draft.txt.content: Report: organized files are easier to hand over.

lesson.goal: Put the draft in Reports as report.txt, remove the old name, and read the result.

steps.explanation: mv renames/moves a regular file in this virtual filesystem. -n skips an existing target.
steps.expected: Report exists at its final path.

steps.explanation: A move removes the old name; the directory remains. Check the source location.
Read the final destination after all changes. Either a direct move or an equivalent copy-and-remove approach can pass.
